candidate.title: DSB-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina DSB-Seq schematic: the explanatory double-strand-break icon, Genome DNA input, TdT and biotinylated-dUTP labeling, DNA isolation and random shearing, Capture on streptavidin beads, and the terminal DNA icon. It depicts a single retained route, without alternative target workflows. The initial icon identifies the biological target rather than an additional manipulation. Primary-paper DSB-Seq sections resolve the preparation history and the unexpanded recovery-to-library interface. Operations o_tail, o_shear, and o_capture correspond to labeled image panels; o_recover and o_library are explicitly paper-supported interfaces to the terminal product, not additional labeled diagram panels. Sequencing and genomic alignment are described as the library readout, outside the drawn operation graph.

operations.label: TdT and biotinylated-dUTP
operations.description: Convert the prepared genomic DNA ends into biotin-containing 3-prime tails. TdT is the catalytic component and biotinylated dUTP supplies the incorporated affinity label; neither is a separate sample branch.
operations.mechanism: TdT-mediated 3-prime end tailing with biotin-modified nucleotides, identified in the primary implementation as biotin-16-dUTP.
operations.information_effect: Creates a covalent affinity handle on labelable DNA ends already present in the prepared genomic DNA, while retaining their attached genomic sequence.

operations.label: DNA isolation and random shearing
operations.description: Process already tailed DNA and randomly fragment it by sonication, producing a mixture in which only fragments retaining a labeled end retain that affinity handle. operations.mechanism: Cleanup of labeled DNA followed by sonication; no new labeling reaction is shown after shearing.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the original end label onto a shorter, break-adjacent genomic fragment and introduces random fragment boundaries elsewhere.

operations.label: Illumina library preparation (paper-supported terminal interface)
operations.description: Convert recovered, tail-removed genomic fragments into a sequencing library, including attachment of Illumina adapters. This is a broad terminal interface inferred from the catalogue and paper, not an internally resolved library-preparation block in the drawing.
operations.mechanism: The cited implementation ligates Illumina adapters to the recovered DNA; other routine library-preparation steps remain within this broad operation.
operations.information_effect: The library reads genomic DNA inserts derived from end-enriched fragments. Sequencing and genomic alignment can establish their genomic distribution. The schematic alone does not establish exact cut coordinates or absolute DSB counts. The paper also cautions that break sites in standard DNA preparations may reflect Top2 halted at cell lysis; the biotin handle does not itself prove a break’s cause.
